title: A user can answer Yes to having a region of origin code, leave the code blank and still move on: DR1 stops them and asks for it.

finding.frontend: Choosing Yes reveals the region of origin code box, but nothing requires it. The only checks on the field are that it is at most five characters long; an empty value passes, the page saves and the user goes on to the next question with a Yes on record and no code against it (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:63-82).
finding.prototype: DR1 treats the code as required the moment Yes is chosen. Save and continue with the box empty returns the page with 'There is a problem' at the top and 'Enter the region of origin code' both in the summary and against the field, and the summary link moves focus into the box (app/routes.js:253-259). Answering No skips the question and nothing is asked.
finding.difference: Make the region of origin code mandatory whenever the requirement radio is Yes, with the error message 'Enter the region of origin code' in the summary and against the field. This is the same conditional-obligation shape the frontend already uses elsewhere, so it is a validator change on one page rather than a new pattern. Leave the No branch alone.
finding.falsifiedBy: Submitting DR1's origin page with Yes selected and the code box empty and reaching the next screen.

relatedTo.why: both change the same revealed field
